title: Arabic for Non-Arabic Speakers – Level 02
overview: This elementary-level course builds on the Arabic alphabet, essential vocabulary and simple expressions introduced in Level 01. Learners strengthen their ability to understand and participate in routine conversations, read short practical texts and write connected sentences. Through structured language practice and realistic situations, participants develop greater accuracy with common verb forms, sentence patterns, questions and everyday interactions in Arabic-speaking communities and workplaces.
audience: Non-Arabic-speaking learners who have completed Arabic Level 01 or demonstrate equivalent foundational proficiency.
Expatriate residents and professionals seeking more independent communication in daily life.
Customer-facing and administrative employees interacting with Arabic-speaking colleagues and clients.
Learners preparing for the broader conversational and reading demands of Arabic Level 03.
methodology: Interactive instructor-led lessons; guided listening and pronunciation practice; structured grammar discovery; vocabulary recycling; paired conversations and role plays; short authentic-style readings; controlled-to-free writing exercises; situational simulations; formative quizzes; and regular feedback on accuracy, fluency and comprehension.
competencies: Understanding the main points of short, clearly delivered conversations on familiar subjects.
Conducting routine exchanges involving requests, preferences, directions and arrangements.
Using present and common past-time structures in basic connected sentences.
Reading practical notices, messages, short descriptions and simple dialogues.
Writing brief messages and paragraphs about familiar experiences and routines.
Applying elementary vocabulary, grammar and culturally appropriate expressions with greater confidence.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Initiate, maintain and close short conversations about everyday needs and experiences.
Ask follow-up questions and respond with information beyond isolated words or memorized phrases.
Describe daily routines, current activities and selected past events using appropriate common structures.
Give and understand simple directions, instructions, requests and appointments.
Read short practical texts and identify their main ideas and key details.
Write connected sentences, messages and short descriptions with appropriate word order.
Use common adjectives, possessive expressions, prepositions and question forms more accurately.
Communicate politely in routine social and workplace situations.
